title: Clinical trial of colchicine to reduce coronary artery inflammation in people with HIV.
official: A randomised, double-blind, multicenter, placebo-controlled clinical trial of colchicine to reduce coronary artery inflammation in people with HIV. COLCOHIV
summary: Main objective: To assess the impact of colchicine versus placebo in reducing coronary artery inflammation in PWH over 50 years and high cardiovascular risk after 96 weeks
conditions: High cardiovascular risk in HIV patients
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. PWH > 50 years old
2. High cardiovascular risk measured by SCORE-2 > 5%
3. Stable antiretroviral therapy (ART) in the previous six months
4. Viral load < 50 copies/mililiter for at least 1 year. One blip is allowed (Viral load between 20-200 copies/mililiter with a previous and after viral load determinations < 20 copies per mililiter.
5. CD4 cell count > 350 cells/mm3
6. Stable dose of an intermediate or high intensity statin in the previous year (statin dose should not be modified throghout the study unless there is a robust clinical indication). In case the participant does not receive statins, all other hypolipemiants (bempedoic acid, ezetimibe) will need to be at a stable dose as well in the previous year.
7. No clinical indication for a change in treatment based on European Society of Cardiology Guidelines
8. Written informed consent obtained according to international guidelines and local laws
9. Ability to understand the nature of the trial and the trial related procedures and to comply with them
Exclusion criteria:
1. Severe Heart failure defined as LVEF < 35%.
2. Renal dysfunctions defined as eGFR < 50 ml/min or serum creatinine levels > 1.7 mg/dL
3. Severe hepatic impairments defined as a Child-Pugh category C
4. Levels of ALT over five times the upper limit of normal OR levels of ALT over three times the upper limit of normal AND bilirrubin levels over one point five times the upper limit of normal
5. Participant is receiving drugs that inhibit the CYP3A4 (e.g. Verapamil, Azithromycin, Clarithromycin, protease inhibitors, cobicistat), CYP2D6 or inhibitors of P-glycoprotein.
6. Participant needs treatment with colchicine for any indication
7. Participants with stomach ulcers or gastrointestinal bleeding
8. Participants with highly elevated hsCRP > 10 mg/dL at screening
9. Women of childbearing potential. - Permanent sterilisation methods including hysterectomy, bilateral salpingectomy and bilateral oophorectomy. -	Postmenopausal state, defined as no menses for 12 months without an alternative medical cause. A high follicle stimulating hormone (FSH) level in the postmenopausal range may be used to confirm a post-menopausal state in women not using hormonal contraception or hormonal replacement therapy. However in the absence of 12 months of amenorrhea, a single FSH measurement is insufficient. -	Male participants are considered fertile after puberty unless permanently sterile by bilateral orchiectomy. To prevent pregnancies in female partners of male participants, they must agree to use highly effective contraceptive methods or have practiced sexual abstinence during the treatment period and until the end of relevant systemic exposure, defined as 5 half-lives of the IMP (9 days approximately).
10. Known hypersensitivity to the active substances or any of the excipients
11. Known iodine contrast allergy with prior history of anaphylaxis
12. Patient without legal capacity who is unable to understand the nature, significance and consequences of the trial
13. Previous MI, stroke or coronary by-pass surgery
14. History of non-cutaneus malignancy prior to enrollment
15. History of inflammatory bowel disease or chronic diarrhoea
